page: Microsoft Azure L4s is a virtual machine instance from the LS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, configured with 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs. The CPU includes 48 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache, with support for AVX, AVX512F, AES, and FMA instructions. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a 694 GB volume that is Premium Storage capable, while no GPU hardware is included.

Benchmark data reveals moderate memory performance and weaker compute capabilities. Large-block memory bandwidth tests show average performance, with read speeds at 50.82 GB/sec and write speeds at 33.22 GB/sec, though small-block cached reads are weaker at 301.97 GB/sec. CPU-bound benchmarks indicate limitations, with stress-ng single-core performance in the bottom 10% (880.27) and multi-core performance in the bottom 25% (3173.22). Similarly, Passmark CPU and database operations fall into the bottom 25%, indicating that the instance is not optimized for heavy compute or high-intensity database transactions. However, it maintains average performance in Redis SET operations (6.03 million operations per second) and small-model LLM inference.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L4s instance offers a high ratio of memory and local storage relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for workloads that require moderate memory capacity and local disk caching without demanding high CPU performance. The combination of 32.0 GB of RAM and 694 GB of local storage suits workloads such as caching layers, lightweight database hosting, Redis deployments, and basic text or image processing tasks. It is less suitable for intensive software compilation, large-scale LLM inference, or high-throughput web serving due to its constrained CPU and multi-core performance.
description: Microsoft Azure L4s is an x86_64 virtual machine from the LS family, powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 4 physical cores. It features 32.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per core) and 694 GB of Premium Storage capable local storage, with no GPU. Benchmarks indicate average performance in large-block memory bandwidth (50.82 GB/sec read) and Redis SET operations (6.03 million operations/sec), but weaker results in CPU-intensive tasks, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core performance falling into the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. This resource profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-centric and storage-cached workloads that do not require heavy compute. It is best suited for caching layers, lightweight databases, Redis deployments, and moderate text or image processing.
